title: Retractions of etale covers imply strict henselianity at maximal ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Suppose that for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ such that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], there is an $A$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:B\to A$ with $\rho\circ(A\to B)=\mathrm{id}_A$. Then for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Here etale for a ring map means etale for its induced morphism of affine schemes; such a ring map is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

theorem IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing.localization_atPrime_of_forall_retraction
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (H : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B], Algebra.Etale A B →
      Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)) →
      ∃ f : B →+* A, f.comp (algebraMap A B) = RingHom.id A)
    (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] :
    IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

A ring retraction is precisely an A-algebra homomorphism to A. Algebra.Etale includes finite presentation; no extra hypothesis is imposed.
